key_insight: A temporally structured Bayesian network can link early type 2 diabetes detection and first-year glycemic control to later cardiovascular disease risk, enabling interpretable risk stratification.
clinical_relevance: In primary care populations with type 2 diabetes, early post-diagnosis signals such as elevated HbA1c may help identify patients at higher cardiovascular risk for closer monitoring.
method: Learned an order-based Bayesian network from longitudinal EHR data on 9,450 primary care patients (2017–2023).
Modeled dependencies among demographics, diagnostic delay surrogates, glycemic control, and post-diagnosis cardiovascular disease outcomes.
Used percentile-based risk groups to compare low-risk and high-risk predicted probabilities.
evidence_signal: The model showed clear risk separation in the abstract, including first-year CVD risk estimates from 5.2% in the low-risk group to 28.9% in the high-risk group, with performance reported as comparable to conventional machine learning.
watch_item: Because the model is trained on retrospective EHR data and uses proxy measures for diagnostic delay, results may not generalize without external validation and careful implementation.
paper_title: Order-Based Bayesian Network Modeling of Early Detection and Post-Diagnosis Control for Cardiovascular Disease Risk in Type 2 Diabetes
